title: The role of ChatGPT in education: Applications, challenges: insights from a systematic review
venue: Journal of Information Technology Education: Research
extended_summary:
This paper conducts a systematic literature review of empirical studies on the use of ChatGPT in school and higher education. The review asks how ChatGPT is being used by teachers and students, what its performance is across subject areas, what limitations and ethical issues arise, and what impact it has on student performance, higher-order thinking, motivation, and related outcomes.

Using PRISMA, the authors searched major academic databases for studies published between January 2023 and January 2024 and screened 1,653 records down to 50 included empirical articles. The review covers preschool, primary, secondary, and higher education, with most evidence coming from higher education and foreign language learning, but with a substantial subset of K-12 studies as well. Reported uses include lesson planning, quiz and assessment creation, personalized materials, dialogue practice, writing support, problem-solving assistance, and grading support.

The review finds that ChatGPT can support cognitive performance, critical thinking, motivation, language learning, and some subject-specific tasks, but its performance is uneven. Limitations and risks include inaccurate or superficial responses, fabricated references, weak deep reasoning, calculation errors in STEM, biased content, privacy concerns, academic integrity violations, copyright issues, overdependence, and potential misuse. The authors conclude that ChatGPT has educational promise, but its integration requires AI literacy, prompt engineering, human oversight, and further empirical research, especially in primary and secondary education.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI’s generative conversational AI chatbot / large language model used to generate, revise, explain, and evaluate text and other educational content.
identified_tools.use_case: This systematic review examined empirical studies using ChatGPT in school and higher education, including its use by teachers for lesson plans, quizzes, rubrics, assessment tasks, and personalized materials, and by students for language practice, feedback, problem-solving, and writing support.

findings.finding_summary: Across the 50 included empirical studies, ChatGPT was reported to support cognitive performance, critical thinking, motivation, language skills, and AI literacy in many contexts, including K-12 settings. However, the review also identified recurring limitations and risks, especially for K-12 classrooms: inaccurate or superficial responses, fabricated citations, reduced higher-order thinking, academic integrity violations, copyright concerns, bias, privacy issues, dependence, and occasional negative effects on academic achievement, critical reasoning, and motivation in one study.
findings.measure: Systematic review synthesis of reported effects and limitations across included empirical studies

findings.finding_summary: The review reports positive effects on language-related outcomes in school and higher education, including improved essay writing, vocabulary and grammar practice, feedback use, and writing improvement. These benefits were especially visible in foreign language learning contexts such as English, German, and Chinese.
findings.measure: Reported language and writing outcomes across included studies

findings.finding_summary: In STEM-related studies, ChatGPT was reported to help students with conceptual understanding and problem-solving, particularly in mathematics, physics, chemistry, and programming. The review also notes important limitations in complex or numerical calculations, with several studies reporting computational errors.
findings.measure: Reported STEM learning outcomes and problem-solving performance

findings.finding_summary: Several studies in the review reported increased motivation, engagement, persistence, and enjoyment when students used ChatGPT. These outcomes were observed in history, data science, programming, business administration, and English learning contexts.
findings.measure: Motivation, engagement, persistence, and enjoyment reports

findings.finding_summary: The review found repeated reports of improved critical thinking and higher-order thinking when ChatGPT was used in structured ways, including knowledge construction, lesson planning, and writing tasks. At the same time, the paper stresses that the model can be limited in deep, creative, and complex problem-solving and may weaken critical thinking if used dependently.
findings.measure: Critical thinking / higher-order thinking outcomes reported in included studies

findings.finding_summary: The review identifies substantial ethical and institutional concerns: academic integrity violations, copyright infringement, privacy risks, biased content, unequal access, and potential malicious use. It also reports concerns about inaccurate student evaluation and shortcomings in curriculum design when ChatGPT is used for grading or instructional planning.
findings.measure: Reported ethical, privacy, assessment, and curriculum-design concerns

quality_tier_rationale: This is a systematic review of empirical studies rather than a single controlled intervention, so the evidence is useful but indirect. The included studies are mostly qualitative, mixed-method, or exploratory, and the paper does not provide pooled effect sizes.
impact_tier_rationale: The review reports many positive educational uses, but the magnitude of effects is not quantified in aggregate and several important risks are emphasized. Because the evidence is synthesis-level and effects are not numerically estimated, impact is best treated as modest/unclear rather than strong.
